preceding_agent.bottleneck: A candidate momentum effect may depend on market regime even after horizon robustness.
preceding_agent.next: The volatility gate research question is resolved: a past-only volatility filter does NOT provide robustness improvement for momentum; the existing MA regime filters and this volatility gate both fail to solve the regime-dependence problem, narrowing the frontier to alternative regime-separation mechanisms.
preceding_agent.objective: Test one explicitly predeclared past-only volatility gate on lookback-5 momentum through the existing regime-stability and null framework.
preceding_agent.observed_effect: The past-only volatility gate eliminated the regime-dependent edge on JPM (pure momentum showed REGIME_DEPENDENT with edge in 2009-2013 turbulent block, volatility-gated showed CONSISTENT_WITH_NOISE across all segments). The gate did NOT improve robustness; it falsified the hypothesis that volatility classification can separate period-specific momentum effects from robust regime-independent edges.
preceding_agent.question: Does a single past-only volatility gate create a predeclared robustness improvement for the qualified momentum effect?
preceding_agent.research_result: Volatility-gated momentum (predeclared vol_threshold=0.25) produces CONSISTENT_WITH_NOISE across AMZN/JPM + 10-asset universe, falsifying the hypothesis that a past-only volatility gate creates robustness. Pure momentum remains REGIME_DEPENDENT (JPM) despite the gate, showing volatility classification cannot separate period-specific edges from robust regime-independent effects.
preceding_agent.uncertainty_reduced: The gate definitively falsifies the candidate: past-only volatility filters cannot resolve regime-dependent momentum edges, confirming that the existing MA regime filters (which failed) are not the unique barrier to regime-robust momentum.
